items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: Who do you think is the best drummer that you ever played with? ... Henry Martin. Henry Martin. ... Henry Martin was a metronome.

ctx.x: his feet. Really? Yeah. He was all pounding the drum and everyone else. Well the drum didn't record you know. Didn't record huh? Yeah. Ben Borders was your drummer. He was a pretty good drummer wasn't he? Fair. Fair. He's my owner.

I'm a bop style drummer you know. Oh yeah? Didn't have much beat on the bass drum. Who do you think is the best drummer that you ever played with? You ever had my band? Yeah. Henry Martin. Henry Martin. And the next Ed Robinson boy started out with him. Might have to pull a straw between the two of them but still I thought. They were both great huh? Henry Martin was a metronome. You couldn't move him after you stomp your feet. Couldn't make him go faster. He couldn't make him go slower. He was really steady huh?…

That's hot. They're barbecue. It's very good. Thank you. Wonderful. Listen. So when did you go to Chicago? 1925. Were you here all the way until 25? Los Angeles. In Los Angeles or here huh? Between here and Los Angeles.

items.title: Manuel "Fess" Manetta and Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1958-08-26
items.q: The best time keeping drummer I ever had, ever played, was with Hendrick Martin.

ctx.x: Yeah, much time. No, very good. He really liked him, huh? The best time keeping drummer I ever had, ever played, was with Hendrick Martin. Yeah, he'd been to your drummer for years. Oh boy. Guy had an idea. Any number you'd play with, any little funny lyrics to it or something, that would mean a bird or a rabbit or a rat, anything, he'd get some kind of instrument to imitate it, you know. A little track. Yeah, fill in, you know. Like a cow, you know. Good coloration. Yeah. Oh yeah, a big bag full of that stuff.…
Well, just one second. I was going to ask, I'll finish up to the Henry Martin business. How come he wasn't with you? Did he live long or was he dead by that time?
He was working in Storoville quite a while with Manuel Perez. He worked with me when, you know, he was on there one night, you see.
